correctness.rationale: For M>=2, the endemic equation is degree M with leading coefficient -s_M/M!<0. Between two attracting roots an intervening equilibrium is necessary, proving at most ceil(M/2) stable. With epsilon rational in (0,min(1/8,eta/4)), delta=epsilon/[4(2M)^(M-1)] and Q=prod(x-j delta/M), all rate coefficients lambda_j remain positive because sum absolute coefficients of Q is <2. At t_j=(j+1/2)delta/M, the perturbation epsilon(1-t_j)Q(t_j) exceeds t_j^M in magnitude by factor >=4(1-delta)>1, forcing M alternating interior/boundary sign changes and exactly M simple roots. Their crossings provide exactly ceil(M/2) attractors and root simplicity gives robustness. Standard-library exact-rational verification for M=2..12 supports the algebra but is not the general proof.

value.rationale: This directly answers the primary source's stated prospect of arbitrarily many positive endemic equilibria from increasing simplex order. It obtains the exact sharp reachable number, optimal stable count, strict positivity at every order, arbitrarily near-unit normalized rates and open robust parameter sets, proving an order-dependent multistability capacity rather than a narrow computed special case. The result is only deterministic mean-field and should not be misread as finite-population persistence.
